predecessors.name: Jin dynasty (Jurchen Jin)
predecessors.text: Liaodong, held by the Khitan rebel Yelu Liuge

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: Liaodong, held by the Khitan rebel Yelu Liuge

ledger.x: 1213: 'Yelu Liuge proclaimed himself king', dynastic name Liao, era name Yuantong (1213-1220).
1214 (the page's paragraph): 'Yelu Liuge established his capital at modern-day Kaiyuan, Liaoning', renamed Zhongjing; the sentence is undated.
1214: 'The Jin dynasty once again attacked Eastern Liao under the command of Puxian Wannu' (the Eastern Xia page: the Jin sent Wannu to Liaodong, 'defeated around Kaiyuan').

1215: Puxian Wannu 'himself rebelled against Jin and founded the Eastern Xia kingdom in Dongjing (Liaoyang) of Jin in 1215'; 'In 1215, Yelu Liuge occupied the eastern capital of the Jin dynasty' (the pages do not reconcile the two statements).
1216: 'Yelu Sibu (the younger brother of Yelu Liuge) rebelled against the pro-Mongol faction', founding Later Liao.
Spring 1219: 'the Later Liao ruler Yelu Hanshe committed suicide', ending Later Liao; Eastern Liao attacked it 'with Mongol and Goryeo support'.
1269: 'The Yuan dynasty abolished the title, ending the Eastern Liao kingdom.'

wars.name: Jin attack on Eastern Liao
wars.outcome: 1214: the Jin attacked Eastern Liao under Puxian Wannu and was defeated around Kaiyuan; in 1215 Wannu rebelled and founded the Eastern Xia, and Liuge occupied Dongjing.

wars.name: Eastern Liao war against the Later Liao
wars.outcome: 1216: Yelu Sibu rebelled against the pro-Mongol faction; spring 1219: the Later Liao ruler Hanshe committed suicide after Eastern Liao attacked with Mongol and Goryeo support.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary or the land held after 1215; Liaoning is a reading.

sources.title: Mongol conquest of the Jin dynasty
